notes: Top-line: mid-market product analytics company building in-app conversational support + personalized recommendations.
Started with Hosted API to validate model quality, then ran short Dedicated POC to validate tail latency and autoscaling behavior.
Customer feedback on POC: "model quality = good; tail latency during cold-starts needs mitigation"
Key ask: committed capacity with predictable overage caps and clear ramp path over first 6 months.
- Customer prefers commit defined as 'committed GPU-hours per month' rather than 'rps' (engineering comfort).
- Initial target commit: equivalent of 3xA100-class nodes (model mix: 70% text-gen chat, 30% embeddings/rerank).
- Requested burst to 6 nodes during product launches; want burst to be billed via a predictable overage ladder (tiered GPU-hour price, capped monthly spend).
- Proposed ramp schedule from customer: Month1 = 50% commit, Month2 = 75%, Month3+ = 100% of committed baseline. Wants price protection during ramp.
AE notes: asked for a concession on ramp months (first 2 months 50% billing) — Redwood to consider a 30% ramp discount for months 1-2.
Legal asks: data residency for EU customers (they have EU customers), KMS integration required for encryption-at-rest, retention policy 90 days for logs, longer for audit export.
SE notes (Priya): recommend configured prefix caching + small KV caching window to reduce token spend and improve tail latency.
Procurement is pushing back on minimum term length; they like 12-month committed price but want ability to scale down after month 6 with 60 day notice.
Competitor concerns: they evaluated OpenAI for hosted quality; Anthropic offered a lower unit price but no dedicated reserved pools + less observability.
Important quote from Head of Platform: "We need predictable bills around product launch spikes — bursts can't create runaway charges."
Next doc to deliver: final SOW with committed GPU-hours table, overage tier table (per GPU-hour), and explicit ramp billing schedule.
